beats.text: He painted the king for 37 years. Then he painted himself.
beats.say: He painted the king for thirty-seven years. Then he painted himself.

beats.text: Diego Velázquez was born in Seville in 1599. As a young man he painted the street: cooks, beggars, a water seller.
beats.say: Diego Velázquez was born in Seville in fifteen ninety-nine. As a young man he painted the street: cooks, beggars, a water seller.

beats.text: At twenty-four, he got one sitting with the young king, Philip the Fourth. The king was thrilled.
Velázquez became court painter, with a promise: no one else would ever paint the king.
He painted Spain's victories, like Breda. The winner doesn't humiliate the loser. He puts a hand on his shoulder.
But the wars drained the treasury. In 1640, Catalonia and Portugal rose up. Portugal was gone for good.
beats.say: But the wars drained the treasury. In sixteen-forty, Catalonia and Portugal rose up. Portugal was gone for good.

beats.text: In Rome he painted the Pope so honestly that, the story goes, the Pope said: too true.
Then came his masterpiece. A little princess, her maids, a dwarf, a sleepy dog.
In the mirror at the back: the king and queen. As if they stood right where you are.
And on the left, brush in hand, Velázquez himself. On his chest, a red cross of knighthood.
But he was only made a knight in 1659, three years later. Someone painted the cross in afterwards.
beats.say: But he was only made a knight in sixteen fifty-nine, three years later. Someone painted the cross in afterwards.

beats.text: He died the next summer. Spain's empire was fading. His paintings never did.
